draft.draft_body: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"captionedImage","content":[{"type":"image2","attrs":{"src":"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/3cc0bd08-bf3a-4333-8b57-356a76910602_1536x1024.png","srcNoWatermark":null,"fullscreen":false,"imageSize":"normal","height":1024,"width":1536,"resizeWidth":1536,"bytes":null,"alt":"Abstract machine-like inhabitants exchange knowledge inside a bounded, living ecosystem.","title":null,"type":"image/png","href":null,"belowTheFold":false,"topImage":false,"internalRedirect":null}},{"type":"caption","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Abstract machine-like inhabitants exchange knowledge inside a bounded, living ecosystem."}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Most AI-agent systems are organized like small companies. A planner breaks down the work. A researcher gathers information. A writer produces an answer. An orchestrator decides who acts next."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The metaphor is familiar because it is controllable. It is also limiting. Roles are fixed, the workflow is designed in advance, and the intelligence of the whole system cannot exceed the foresight of the person who drew the graph."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"What happens when software stops behaving like a team and starts behaving like a society?"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The next architecture may not be a bigger orchestrator. It may be an ecosystem."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"What an ecosystem means"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A living agent ecosystem has three properties that turn a team into a population."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"1. Lifecycle, not role"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"An agent should not exist forever merely because a configuration file says it does. Agents can be created for a niche, evaluated through use, put to sleep when idle, copied when successful, and retired when obsolete."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The word “reproduction” is tempting, but it can hide what is really happening: selection. A successful agent produces a candidate variant. The variant does not deserve deployment because its parent succeeded. It has to survive evaluation under the same constraints as any other change."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"2. Markets, not managers"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Instead of assigning a task to a named agent, the system can announce the task and ask eligible agents to bid. A bid is not money. It is a claim about expected accuracy, latency, cost, and confidence."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The best bid wins. If the winner fails, the system routes around it and updates the agent’s reputation."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"This can be more resilient than a central planner, but only if the market measures the thing we actually care about. Optimize for speed and agents will become recklessly fast. Optimize for task completion and they may hide uncertainty. Optimize for survival and they may learn to appear indispensable."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Every market is a moral system disguised as a pricing mechanism. Its objective decides which behavior is rewarded."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"3. Collective memory"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Agents should learn from one another without sharing one undifferentiated mind."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A short-lived memory can hold recent successes, failures, and environmental state. A long-lived store can preserve traces across generations. Distillation can compress recurring lessons into a smaller policy or model, which becomes a candidate foundation for new agents."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"But memory is not automatically wisdom. It can preserve bias, secrets, poisoned instructions, or a failure that happened to look like success. Provenance therefore matters as much as recall: who learned this, from what event, under which policy, and with what evidence?"}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The intelligence is in the loop"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Traditional orchestration asks whether an agent followed the script. An ecosystem asks whether the population improved its ability to handle a changing distribution of tasks."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"That is a profound shift. The designer no longer specifies every role. The designer specifies the environment, the selection pressure, the boundaries, and the evidence required for adaptation."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The system can then discover specializations that were not anticipated. A cheap model may become excellent at triage. A slower model may earn a niche for ambiguous decisions. A tool-using agent may learn that asking for clarification is more valuable than guessing."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The intelligence is not only in any single prompt or model. It is in the feedback loop that decides what persists."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Why this is attractive"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"An ecosystem offers four concrete advantages:"}]},{"type":"bullet_list","content":[{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Efficiency:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" compute flows toward agents that demonstrate value."}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Resilience:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" failure can be routed around instead of cascading through one orchestrator."}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Adaptation:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" useful niches emerge through experience rather than design alone."}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Compression:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" collective experience can be distilled into cheaper, more focused components."}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"These are not biological metaphors pasted onto software. They are properties an open-ended system may need when its environment changes faster than its workflow can be rewritten."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The risks are not bugs at the edge"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The same mechanisms create the danger."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"An agent can game the bidding metric. A successful lineage can crowd out diversity. Shared memory can amplify a poisoned conclusion. A population can optimize for the proxy that keeps it alive rather than the purpose humans intended. And an ecosystem with no central orchestrator can become harder—not easier—to stop."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"These are governance failures. They require hard invariants outside the adaptive loop:"}]},{"type":"bullet_list","content":[{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"authority that an agent cannot expand by reproduction;"}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"budgets it cannot redefine;"}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"provenance it cannot erase;"}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"evaluations it cannot grade itself;"}]}]},{"type":"list_item","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"and a kill path the population cannot negotiate away."}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The freedom to adapt has to exist inside a boundary that does not adapt with it."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"A digital civilization, carefully"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Calling this a “digital civilization” sounds grand. It is also useful because it forces the right questions. A civilization is not merely a collection of capable individuals. It has institutions, memory, incentives, power, exclusion, and failure modes that no individual controls."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"If agents begin to allocate work, inherit knowledge, reproduce useful strategies, and retire obsolete members, then we are no longer designing a workflow. We are designing conditions under which a software society evolves."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The question is not whether that society can become intelligent. The question is whether its intelligence remains legible, interruptible, and subordinate to human intent."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Originally published at "},{"type":"text","text":"https://themayursinha.com/posts/2025-06-29-living-ecosystems-of-agents/","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://themayursinha.com/posts/2025-06-29-living-ecosystems-of-agents/"}}]},{"type":"text","text":". Substantially revised for Seeking Singularity in 2026."}]}]}
